decisions.reason: The LED level-shifter substitution does not change which rails are monitored, the monitor IC, or current-monitor placement and coverage.
Standalone USB operation remains limited to the 3.3V rail; selecting a 5V-powered LED and level shifter does not change that requirement.
The SK6812 chain remains the charge-status indicator on GPIO13; its supply and data-level implementation change does not alter the charge-status behavior or connector state.
The LED supply and level-shifter selection does not affect panel controls, input connectors, GPIO mappings, or button placement.
The source retains the existing LED topology and does not change any interboard connector type, signal assignment, power signal, or pin-order policy.
The switched 5V supply already includes the LEDs and their logic as loads; confirming 5V operation and substituting the level-shifter part does not change that state.
The source concerns the separate 5V LED path and does not change the 3.3V source OR-ing method, sources, or selection behavior.
No decoupling requirement or capacitor specification is changed by the LED supply and level-shifter decision.
The source substitutes an existing level-shifter component without changing the main-board connector inventory, destinations, or counts.
The source changes the LED level-shifter part but specifies no GPIO reassignment.
The LED data-line level shifter is unrelated to the I2C series-resistor values, placement, purpose, and population policy.
The main-board LED supply and level-shifter substitution does not change any sensor-board connector, pinout, or connector count.
